# E129 -- Dreher

## Metadata
- **Organization:** Dreher Birra (Dreher Beer, Italy)
- **Year:** Estimated late 1960s--1970s (scanned from physical spiral-bound manual; PDF created 2018 as digitization)
- **Sector:** Beer / Beverage (FMCG)
- **Pages:** 41 (including blank endpapers)
- **Design Agency:** Not credited (likely a major Italian design consultancy of the era; quality suggests Unimark or comparable firm)
- **Format Quality:** Digitized scan of a physical spiral-bound corporate identity manual. Custom page size (913.5x648 pts, landscape). All text is outlined/image-based -- no extractable text. High-resolution photography of product applications. 138 MB file. Language: Italian throughout ("Immagine aziendale" = Corporate Image).

## Brand Strategy
The introduction (page 4, in Italian) presents this as a comprehensive corporate image program ("immagine aziendale"). It frames the corporate identity as a tool for communication consistency across all touchpoints -- reflecting the Unimark/Swiss-influenced corporate identity philosophy dominant in Italian design of the 1960s-70s. The guide positions the brand mark as the central unifying element across an extensive product and distribution system. Founded 1865 (referenced in the wheat/date emblem).

## Logo
- **Primary mark:** Rounded-square shield shape containing "Dreher" in blackletter script over a red field, with a small wheat/cross emblem, and "BIRRA" in expressive italicized lettering below
- **Geometric construction:** Extraordinarily detailed construction drawings show the precise geometric basis of the rounded-square shield shape using grid systems, compass arcs, and mathematical relationships (page 6)
- **Wordmark elements:** "DREHER" also appears in a clean sans-serif logotype (visible on signage and vehicles) as a secondary/simplified mark
- **Supporting elements documented separately:**
  - Wheat sheaf with "1865" date and ribbon emblem (heritage mark)
  - "BIRRA" word in distinctive perspective/italic treatment
- **Signage variants:** Metal signage in two standard formats; directional sign with arrow; illuminated highway billboard application
- **Billboard signage:** Modular system showing various configurations of logo mark + "BIRRA DREHER" text for vertical billboards

## Typography
- **Blackletter:** The "Dreher" name in the primary mark uses a style described as being based on "Fette Gotisch" (referenced on page 6), a traditional German blackletter appropriate to the brand's Central European brewing heritage (Anton Dreher was Austrian-Hungarian)
- **Sans-serif logotype:** "DREHER" in a bold geometric sans-serif for secondary applications (signage, vehicles, crates)
- **"BIRRA" lettering:** Custom perspective/italic display lettering
- **Detailed letterform construction:** Pages 12-13 show individual letter construction drawings for "BIRRA" and "DREHER" -- each letter (A, D, R, E) mapped on a grid with geometric construction lines showing precise curves, proportions, and mathematical relationships. This level of typographic engineering is remarkable.
- **Body text:** The manual itself uses a clean Helvetica-style sans-serif for all descriptive text

## Color
- **Primary red:** Vivid warm red for the upper portion of the shield mark (the dominant brand color)
- **Black:** Used for the shield outline, blackletter wordmark, and all secondary applications
- **White:** Background of the lower shield portion and text applications
- **Gold/Kraft:** Visible in packaging applications (cardboard brown tones for multi-pack carriers)
- No formal color specification system visible (predates Pantone standardization in European markets; likely specified via printing ink references in the original)

## Graphics
- The rounded-square shield is the core graphic device, functioning simultaneously as logo container, label shape, and signage element
- The wheat sheaf / 1865 date / ribbon emblem serves as a heritage graphic element
- Extensive technical drawings throughout -- the guide reads like an engineering specification document, with red construction lines, dimension callouts in millimeters, and cross-section views
- No pattern system or decorative graphics

## Photography
- Product photography on dark/black backgrounds for bottles, six-packs, and packaging variants (page 25) -- studio-lit, professional product shots
- Environmental photography: one notable nighttime highway image showing illuminated Dreher billboard against light-trail traffic (page 17) -- atmospheric brand-in-context documentation
- No photography guidelines per se; photographs document existing applications rather than prescribe a style

## Applications
Exceptionally comprehensive application coverage, including:
- **Stationery:** Letterhead, envelope, and business card system (page 20, "materiale di cancelleria" from the Trieste factory)
- **Signage:** Standard metal signs in two sizes; directional arrow sign; modular billboard configurations; illuminated highway signage
- **Vehicle livery:** Detailed technical drawings for multiple vehicle types:
  - Fiat 600 T van (front, side, rear views with precise placement dimensions)
  - Fiat 1100 T van
  - Tigrotto OM delivery truck with pallet transport
  - Fiat 682 semi-trailer truck (full-length side branding)
  - All vehicles shown with exact measurements in millimeters
- **Packaging:** Bottle labels, six-pack carriers, cardboard cases (24-bottle and 16-bottle crate variants with technical construction drawings)
- **Bottle/glass design:** Technical construction drawings of the beer glass ("bicchiere normale") and draft beer tap head ("testa da birra") with precise dimensional specifications
- **Point of sale:** Referenced in TOC as "Capitolo 7: Pubblicita nel punto di vendita"

## Tone of Voice
Not applicable in the modern sense. The manual is written in formal Italian technical/corporate language. No brand voice, messaging, or copywriting guidelines are included -- consistent with the era's focus on visual identity systems over verbal identity.

## Outliers
- **Era and provenance:** This is a genuine mid-century Italian corporate identity manual, likely from the late 1960s or early 1970s -- a historically significant document from the golden age of European corporate identity programs
- **Engineering precision:** The level of technical specification is extraordinary by any era's standards. Letterforms are constructed with geometric precision (compass arcs, grid systems). Vehicle livery includes millimeter-accurate placement specs. Even the beer glass and tap head have engineering drawings. This treats brand identity as industrial design.
- **Spiral-bound physical artifact:** The document was clearly a working reference manual -- the spiral binding, the aged paper visible in scans, and the physical photography suggest this was a production tool, not a presentation piece
- **Blackletter in Italian context:** The use of Fette Gotisch blackletter for an Italian beer brand deliberately signals the Austrian/Central European brewing heritage of Anton Dreher (who founded one of the first lager breweries in 1840s Vienna)
- **Complete absence of digital/text layer:** All content is outlined or photographic -- the 2018 PDF is a faithful scan preservation of the physical document
- **Vehicle-specific specifications:** Different technical drawings for each Fiat vehicle model (600 T, 1100 T, Tigrotto OM, 682) -- showing how seriously physical brand application was taken in pre-digital identity programs

## Quality Score
**4 / 5** -- A masterclass in systematic corporate identity from the mid-century European tradition. The technical precision of the mark construction, letterform engineering, and application specifications is exceptional and historically significant. The comprehensive coverage of physical applications (vehicles, signage, packaging, glassware) reflects the era's priorities perfectly. Points deducted for the absence of color specifications, any verbal/tonal guidelines, and the lack of brand strategy articulation beyond a brief introduction -- though these omissions are characteristic of the period rather than failures of the document. As a historical reference for corporate identity methodology, this is invaluable.
